purpose: Discovery register for potentially useful open industrial-maintenance knowledge and data. It is not an imported fault database.
policy: Do not copy repository contents or datasets into this project until the exact license, dataset terms, attribution requirements, and provenance are checked. Research papers and public GitHub visibility do not by themselves grant redistribution rights. Permissively licensed dataset metadata and candidate snapshots may be stored in isolated research folders with attribution and source evidence; no candidate data is loaded by runtime until separately reviewed and approved.

sources.title: Pump Maintenance — Predictive Maintenance Pipeline
sources.potentialUse: Methodology and leakage-audit reference only; not a root-cause fault knowledge source.
sources.reportedScope: README describes the Kaggle Pump Sensor Data set: 220,320 one-minute rows over about 153 days, 52 sensors, labels NORMAL (205,836), RECOVERING (14,477) and BROKEN (7).
sources.licenseStatus: No repository LICENSE file or GitHub license metadata was found. The external Kaggle dataset's exact license was not reviewed.
sources.accessStatus: README, src/load_data.py, src/health_indicators.py, src/anomaly_detector.py, src/classifier.py and src/evaluate.py inspected. The external sensor.csv is not committed and was not downloaded.
sources.codeLicense: not declared; no repository LICENSE file found
sources.dataLicense: External Kaggle Pump Sensor Data license not independently verified
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed data-loading, rolling-feature construction, anomaly detection, time-based classifier split and metrics-report code. Raw sensor data and generated result artifacts were not present for independent reproduction.
sources.originalDataSource: Kaggle dataset nphantawee/pump-sensor-data, as cited by the repository README.
qualityNotes: The classifier maps both RECOVERING and BROKEN to one positive class; this is state classification, not root-cause identification.
Only seven rows carry the BROKEN label; most positive labels are RECOVERING.
The classifier uses a time-based split, but feature preparation uses bfill on the time series and on test features, creating a potential look-ahead bias that requires a controlled rerun.
README metrics, including near-perfect AUC claims, were not independently reproduced because the source dataset is not included and its license is unresolved.
The Isolation Forest detects deviations; it does not identify the physical failure mechanism.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Python 3.11+ and scientific Python dependencies are described by README; unsuitable for the Android PWA or Worker runtime. Keep any evaluation isolated.
sources.reuseConditions: Do not copy repository code or download/redistribute the Kaggle data until both code and dataset rights are confirmed. Treat reported scores as unverified until rerun with leakage-safe validation.

sources.title: Awesome Bearing Datasets for Diagnostics and Prognostics
sources.potentialUse: Discovery index for selecting bearing benchmarks; each original dataset must be reviewed separately.
sources.reportedScope: Catalogue covers bearing diagnosis and prognostics datasets including CWRU, XJTU-SY, SEU, HUST and Paderborn; README links detailed descriptions and coverage notes.
sources.licenseStatus: Repository LICENSE is MIT for the catalogue repository. The README directs users to datasets hosted by separate institutions; MIT does not grant rights to those datasets.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE and docs/datasets.md inspected. The repository is a catalogue; no raw bearing signals are included in the inspected tree.
sources.dataLicense: Per-dataset and per-originating-institution; not covered by the catalogue's MIT license
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the catalogue structure and selected dataset descriptions, including CWRU, XJTU-SY, SEU, HUST and Paderborn. No raw signals were copied or downloaded.
sources.originalDataSource: Separate originating institutions and repositories listed in docs/datasets.md; each must be checked at its original publisher.
qualityNotes: A discovery catalogue, not a validated dataset and not a fault-case database.
Fault generation differs across datasets (artificial seeded defects versus natural/accelerated run-to-failure).
Sampling rates, sensors, loads and operating conditions are not interchangeable across datasets.
Data leakage and license conditions must be reviewed separately for every selected source.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Do not package the catalogue or raw signals in runtime. Use metadata for offline benchmark selection only after per-dataset review.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT notice applies to repository code/docs; obtain and comply with the original dataset license and attribution for each dataset.

sources.title: FSBrick — HVAC Fault-Symptom Information Model
sources.potentialUse: Reference for representing HVAC fault severity, symptoms and fault-symptom relationships; not a validated diagnostic procedure library.
sources.reportedScope: README describes an information model built on Brick and identifies one Turtle ontology file plus three Excel analysis workbooks.
sources.licenseStatus: Repository LICENSE is MIT. Rights for the three analysis spreadsheets and the derivative Brick_withFSBrick.ttl content were not separately established; the TTL extends the Brick ontology and requires upstream license/provenance review.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE and recursive tree inspected. Brick_withFSBrick.ttl (1,609,629 bytes) and three .xlsx files are present; their payloads were not parsed in this review.
sources.codeLicense: MIT for repository material explicitly covered by LICENSE
sources.dataLicense: Not separately verified for the Excel analysis files; derivative ontology rights require review against the upstream Brick BSD-3-Clause license and source attribution
sources.contentsReviewed: README identifies fault, severity, symptom and fault-symptom relationships. The 1.6 MB TTL and three Excel files were inventoried but not opened or parsed.
sources.originalDataSource: Brick ontology at brickschema.org plus the FSBrick research project and its accompanying paper, DOI 10.1145/3600100.3623729.
qualityNotes: The repository describes an information model, not a general HVAC troubleshooting knowledge base.
No workbook-level provenance, row-level license or data-quality audit was performed.
The derived TTL may include upstream Brick terms; do not assume the repository MIT notice replaces upstream notices.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: A small, manually reviewed and attributed ontology subset could be mapped to JSON. Do not embed the full TTL or spreadsheets in the PWA/Worker.
sources.reuseConditions: Reference the paper and original Brick ontology. Do not copy the TTL or spreadsheets until file-level provenance and all applicable notices are verified.

sources.title: Hydraulic System Condition Monitoring
sources.potentialUse: Evaluation-method reference for the UCI hydraulic benchmark; not a source of general maintenance procedures.
sources.reportedScope: README describes 2,205 hydraulic test-rig cycles for cooler, valve, pump internal leakage and accumulator labels, using 17 sensor channels and statistical/FFT features.
sources.licenseStatus: No repository LICENSE file or GitHub license metadata was found for the code. The underlying UCI dataset is separately licensed CC BY 4.0.
sources.accessStatus: README, src/evaluation.py, reports/data_manifest.json and repository tree inspected. Raw UCI data are downloaded by script and are not embedded in the repository.
sources.codeLicense: not declared; no repository LICENSE file found
sources.dataLicense: UCI Condition Monitoring of Hydraulic Systems dataset CC BY 4.0 (DOI 10.24432/C5CW21); separate from this repository's code
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the training/evaluation split, metrics protocol and manifest with the original UCI archive URL, byte count and SHA-256. The raw archive was not downloaded.
sources.originalDataSource: UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 447, ZeMA; DOI 10.24432/C5CW21.
qualityNotes: The README's reported metrics are model classification scores on laboratory cycle labels, not causal diagnosis or repair guidance.
The evaluation uses a random stratified 80/20 cycle split; the separate ordered-sensitivity analysis is not the primary final split. Group/temporal dependence across cycles is not ruled out.
The manifest provides archive and file hashes, but raw files were not independently re-downloaded in this review.
The repository code has no declared license; do not copy its implementation.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Python 3.12/scientific Python evaluation is suitable only for an isolated benchmark environment; not for Android or Worker runtime.
sources.reuseConditions: Use the original UCI dataset under CC BY 4.0 with attribution if benchmark data are needed; do not copy this repository's code without a separate license.
